basis: Lilly sickness judgment: testimonies of death are stacked and unrelieved — the Ascendant (the sick man's body/life) is most afflicted by the corporal presence of a planet who is partly lord of the eighth (death) in the Ascendant itself; the sign of the sixth is fixed and afflicted and the lord of the sixth sits in a fixed, earthly, melancholy sign = a fixed, earthy, black-choler disease that will not shift; the Sun, the temporal light and significator of vitality, is in perfect opposition of Saturn, lord of the sixth, in fixed signs = the disease significator directly overthrows the light of life on a fixed axis; the Moon, co-significatrix of the patient, is near the Dragon's Tail (Cauda) and afflicted in the Ascendant = light extinguished at the body. No applying benefic, reception, or translation to the lord of the Ascendant is stated to rescue him. Disease quality follows the lord of the sixth: earthly melancholy, cold and dry obstruction/wasting. Verdict by Lilly's rule: death, not recovery.
prediction_text: The sick man will die, not recover. His disease is a fixed, earthly, melancholic (black-choler) affliction — cold, dry, obstructive and wasting in nature — seated by the afflicted fixed sixth house and its lord; with the Ascendant afflicted by a lord of the eighth, the Sun in perfect opposition to Saturn lord of the sixth, and the Moon near the Dragon's Tail afflicted in the Ascendant, the testimonies are of death.
timing: Month scale, near term (figure of 16 July 1645): death within a window of weeks to a few months from the figure; main coordinate in the nearer part of that window, the afflictions being already perfect (opposition already exact, Moon already with Cauda)
